2	# run --verify contract (verify_oracle F4): opt-in oracle cross-check.
3	#   1. hybrid marker --verify  -> oracle leg + "[verify] PASS", rc 0
4	#   2. hybrid pc --verify      -> same through the exit_pc oracle path
5	#   3. default (no --verify)   -> no verify leg, no verify output
6	#   4. --verify with fast/cycle -> usage error (rc 2)
7	#   5. --verify with icount     -> usage error (rc 2)
8	#   6. run --help documents --verify
9	set -uo pipefail
10	
11	SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
12	ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
13	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"
14	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"
15	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/roi.sh"
16	
17	BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
18	bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
19	
20	FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-rt_c_hello}"
21	hybrid_resolve_paths
22	ENGINE="${ENGINE:-vsim:ax45mpv_premium}"
23	
24	# 1. marker mode.
25	OUT=$("$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENGINE" --verify \
26	      "$VSIM_ELF" 2>&1)
27	RC=$?
28	[ "$RC" -eq 0 ] || fail "marker --verify rc=$RC: $OUT"
29	printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q '\[verify\] PASS' || fail "marker: no [verify] PASS: $OUT"
30	printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q '\[state-diff\] PASS' || fail "marker: no state-diff detail: $OUT"
31	printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q 'window_cycles' || fail "marker: cycle figure missing: $OUT"
32	ok "hybrid marker --verify: oracle cross-check PASS"
33	
34	# 2. pc mode (boundaries = the fixture's own marker PCs, like docs 4.2).
35	OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}}"
36	OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}"

38	  || fail "no ROI markers in $VSIM_ELF"

40	      --pc-start "0x${MARKERS%% *}" --pc-end "0x${MARKERS##* }" --verify \
41	      "$VSIM_ELF" 2>&1)
42	RC=$?
43	[ "$RC" -eq 0 ] || fail "pc --verify rc=$RC: $OUT"
44	printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q '\[verify\] PASS' || fail "pc: no [verify] PASS: $OUT"
45	ok "hybrid pc --verify: oracle cross-check PASS"
46	
47	# 3. default off: no oracle leg, no verify output.
48	OUT=$("$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENGINE" \
49	      "$VSIM_ELF" 2>&1)
50	RC=$?
51	[ "$RC" -eq 0 ] || fail "default hybrid rc=$RC: $OUT"
52	printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -qi 'verify' && fail "default run leaked verify output: $OUT"
53	ok "default: verification stays off"

57	  "$BIN" run --mode fast --verify "$VSIM_ELF"
58	expect 2 'verify requires --mode hybrid' \
59	  "$BIN" run --mode cycle --verify "$VSIM_ELF"
60	ok "--verify usage errors (fast/cycle)"
61

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# RED test for F3: `./hsim.py run <elf> --mode marker|pc --kanata FILE`.
3	#
4	# Produces a kanata pipeline log restricted to the ROI region of the
5	# hybrid run. marker-mode auto-derives ROI bounds from the resume PC and
6	# the unique exit-marker PC. pc-mode honors --pc-start/--pc-end.
7	
8	set -uo pipefail
9	
10	SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
11	ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
12	HSIM="$ROOT/hsim.py"
13	
14	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"
15	
16	[ -x "$HSIM" ] || fail "missing executable: $HSIM"
17	
18	# Same convention as tests/lib/paths.sh: fall back to ./config.env when
19	# the toolchain isn't already on the env, so --objdump probing works
20	# without requiring `source ./setup.sh` first.
21	if [ -z "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}" ] && [ -f "$ROOT/config.env" ]; then
22	  . "$ROOT/config.env"
23	fi
24	
25	cd "$ROOT"
26	
27	TMPDIR_ROOT=$(mktemp -d -t hsim-kanata-XXXXXX)
28	trap 'rm -rf "$TMPDIR_ROOT"' EXIT
29	
30	# 1. --help advertises --kanata and --objdump on the run subcommand.
31	out=$("$HSIM" run --help 2>&1) || fail "run --help exit nonzero: $out"
32	echo "$out" | grep -q -- "--kanata"  || fail "run --help missing --kanata:\n$out"
33	echo "$out" | grep -q -- "--objdump" || fail "run --help missing --objdump:\n$out"
34	ok "run --help lists --kanata and --objdump"
35	
36	# 2. --kanata with --mode icount -> rc=2 (the kanata-roi path only supports
37	#    marker/pc).
38	set +e
39	out=$("$HSIM" run tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf --mode icount \
40	       --kanata "$TMPDIR_ROOT/x.kanata" 2>&1); rc=$?
41	set -e
42	[ "$rc" -eq 2 ] || fail "--kanata with icount should rc=2, got $rc:\n$out"
43	echo "$out" | grep -qi "kanata" || fail "icount rejection should mention kanata:\n$out"
44	ok "--kanata + --mode icount rejected (rc=2)"
45	
46	# 3. marker-mode smoke: kanata file is created, non-empty, has Kanata header.
47	KFILE="$TMPDIR_ROOT/marker.kanata"
48	SMOKE_TIMEOUT=60
49	set +e
50	out=$(timeout "$SMOKE_TIMEOUT" "$HSIM" run tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf \
51	        --mode marker --kanata "$KFILE" 2>&1); rc=$?
52	set -e
53	[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "marker-mode kanata run failed rc=$rc; output:\n$out"
54	[ -s "$KFILE" ] || fail "marker-mode: kanata file not created or empty: $KFILE"
55	head -1 "$KFILE" | grep -q "^Kanata" \
56	  || fail "marker-mode: kanata file missing 'Kanata' header (first line):\n$(head -2 "$KFILE")"
57	# ROI window must have at least one fetched insn (I record) and one
58	# retired insn (R record). Both should appear after the LoopGate opens.
59	grep -q "^I	" "$KFILE" \
60	  || fail "marker-mode: kanata file has no I (start_insn) records:\n$(head -20 "$KFILE")"
61	grep -q "^R	" "$KFILE" \
62	  || fail "marker-mode: kanata file has no R (retire_insn) records:\n$(head -20 "$KFILE")"
63	ok "marker-mode --kanata produces a valid kanata trace"
64	
65	# 4. marker-mode with --objdump: a load-line shows the disassembly. This
66	#    proves the OBJDUMP_FILE env reached vsim via e2e.sh.
67	DUMP="$TMPDIR_ROOT/rt_c_hello.S"
68	OBJDUMP_TOOL="${OBJDUMP:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}}"
69	OBJDUMP_TOOL="${OBJDUMP_TOOL:-riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}"
70	if ! command -v "$OBJDUMP_TOOL" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
71	  echo "[skip] objdump not found ($OBJDUMP_TOOL); skipping --objdump check"
72	else
73	  "$OBJDUMP_TOOL" -d tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf > "$DUMP" \
74	    || fail "objdump -d failed for rt_c_hello.elf"
75	  KFILE2="$TMPDIR_ROOT/marker-dump.kanata"
76	  set +e
77	  out=$(timeout "$SMOKE_TIMEOUT" "$HSIM" run tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf \
78	          --mode marker --kanata "$KFILE2" --objdump "$DUMP" 2>&1); rc=$?
79	  set -e
80	  [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "marker+objdump run failed rc=$rc; output:\n$out"
81	  # With objdump, L records should embed the asm text after the PC.
82	  # Example: "L\t1\t0\t0x800000ec: slti  zero,zero,1441"
83	  grep -E "^L\b.*0x[0-9a-f]+: [a-z]" "$KFILE2" >/dev/null \
84	    || fail "marker+objdump: no L record with disassembly text:\n$(head -20 "$KFILE2")"
85	  ok "marker-mode --kanata --objdump embeds disassembly"
86	fi
87	
88	# 5. pc-mode smoke: explicit --pc-start/--pc-end. ROI bounds come from
89	#    the $DUMP written in step 4 (marker encodings: 5a002013 enter and
90	#    5a102013 exit; raw encoding is mnemonic-independent).
91	if [ -s "${DUMP:-}" ]; then
92	  ENTER=$(awk 'matched==0 && /5a002013/{gsub(":","",$1); print $1; matched=1}' "$DUMP")
93	  EXIT=$(awk 'matched==0 && /5a102013/{gsub(":","",$1); print $1; matched=1}' "$DUMP")
94	  if [ -n "${ENTER:-}" ] && [ -n "${EXIT:-}" ]; then
95	    KFILE3="$TMPDIR_ROOT/pc.kanata"
96	    set +e
97	    out=$(timeout "$SMOKE_TIMEOUT" "$HSIM" run tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf \
98	            --mode pc --pc-start "0x$ENTER" --pc-end "0x$EXIT" \
99	            --kanata "$KFILE3" 2>&1); rc=$?
100	    set -e
101	    [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "pc-mode kanata run failed rc=$rc; output:\n$out"
102	    [ -s "$KFILE3" ] || fail "pc-mode: kanata file not created or empty"
103	    head -1 "$KFILE3" | grep -q "^Kanata" \
104	      || fail "pc-mode: missing Kanata header"
105	    grep -q "^I	" "$KFILE3" \
106	      || fail "pc-mode: no I records:\n$(head -20 "$KFILE3")"
107	    ok "pc-mode --kanata produces a valid kanata trace"
108	  else
109	    echo "[skip] could not extract ROI markers from rt_c_hello"
110	  fi
111	fi
112	
113	echo "PASS test_hsim_kanata"

175	    0)  status=PASS ;;
176	    77) status=SKIP ;;
177	    *)  status=FAIL ;;
178	  esac
179	  (
180	    flock 9
181	    case "$status" in
182	      PASS) ok   "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (${elapsed}s)" ;;
183	      SKIP) warn "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (rc=77, ${elapsed}s)" ;;
184	      FAIL) fail "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (rc=$rc, ${elapsed}s) -> $log" ;;

192	# matters: marker-mode tests first, then pc-mode, then negatives (matching
193	# the original sequential layout so logs are streamed in the same order).
194	declare -a WORKPLAN=()
195	for tm in marker pc; do
196	  [[ "$MODE" != "both" && "$MODE" != "$tm" ]] && continue
197	  for entry in "${RT_TESTS[@]}"; do
198	    rt_name="${entry%%|*}"
199	    env_prefix="${entry#*|}"
200	    # B3: anchor the regex so FILTER=rt_csr does not silently also match
201	    # rt_csr_survival. Users who want a substring match pass '.*marker.*'.
202	    [[ -n "$FILTER" && ! "$rt_name" =~ ^$FILTER$ ]] && continue
203	    cmd="TRIGGER_MODE=$tm $env_prefix bash $HARNESS/e2e.sh"
204	    WORKPLAN+=("$tm|$rt_name|$cmd")
205	  done
206	done
207	for entry in "${NEG_TESTS[@]}"; do
208	  neg_name="${entry%%|*}"
209	  neg_cmd="${entry#*|}"
210	  [[ -n "$FILTER" && ! "$neg_name" =~ ^$FILTER$ ]] && continue
211	  WORKPLAN+=("neg|$neg_name|$neg_cmd")
212	done

214	# Serial phase: same (mode, name, cmd) tuples, executed one at a time
215	# after the parallel pool drains (see SERIAL_RT_TESTS above for why).
216	declare -a SERIAL_PLAN=()
217	for tm in marker pc; do
218	  [[ "$MODE" != "both" && "$MODE" != "$tm" ]] && continue
219	  for entry in "${SERIAL_RT_TESTS[@]}"; do
220	    rt_name="${entry%%|*}"
221	    env_prefix="${entry#*|}"
222	    [[ -n "$FILTER" && ! "$rt_name" =~ ^$FILTER$ ]] && continue
223	    cmd="TRIGGER_MODE=$tm $env_prefix bash $HARNESS/e2e.sh"
224	    SERIAL_PLAN+=("$tm|$rt_name|$cmd")
225	  done
226	done

228	TOTAL=$(( ${#WORKPLAN[@]} + ${#SERIAL_PLAN[@]} ))
229	step "logs: $LOG_DIR  jobs: $JOBS  mode: $MODE  tests: $TOTAL"
230	
231	# FIFO-based bounded job pool. Each child reads one token from $SEM_FIFO
232	# before starting and writes one back on exit; only $JOBS tokens exist,
233	# so at most $JOBS children run concurrently. Opening the fifo in
234	# read-write mode (<>) means writes never block the parent. The fifo
235	# inode is unlinked immediately after fd 8 is bound -- the kernel keeps
236	# the pipe alive as long as fd 8 is open.
237	SEM_FIFO="$LOG_DIR/sem.fifo"
238	mkfifo "$SEM_FIFO"
239	exec 8<>"$SEM_FIFO"
240	rm -f "$SEM_FIFO"
241	for ((sem_i=0; sem_i<JOBS; sem_i++)); do
242	  printf '.\n' >&8
243	done
244	
245	i=0
246	for w in "${WORKPLAN[@]}"; do
247	  i=$((i+1))
248	  w_mode="${w%%|*}"
249	  w_rest="${w#*|}"
250	  w_name="${w_rest%%|*}"
251	  w_cmd="${w_rest#*|}"
252	  read -r -u 8 _tok
253	  (
254	    run_one "$w_mode" "$w_name" "$w_cmd" "$i" "$TOTAL"
255	    printf '.\n' >&8
256	  ) &
257	done
258	wait
259	exec 8>&-
260	
261	# Serial phase: each heavyweight test gets the machine to itself.
262	for w in "${SERIAL_PLAN[@]}"; do
263	  i=$((i+1))
264	  w_mode="${w%%|*}"
265	  w_rest="${w#*|}"
266	  w_name="${w_rest%%|*}"
267	  w_cmd="${w_rest#*|}"
268	  run_one "$w_mode" "$w_name" "$w_cmd" "$i" "$TOTAL"
269	done
270	
271	declare -A MODE_PASS=([marker]=0 [pc]=0 [neg]=0)
272	declare -A MODE_FAIL=([marker]=0 [pc]=0 [neg]=0)
273	declare -A MODE_SKIP=([marker]=0 [pc]=0 [neg]=0)
274	declare -a FAILED_NAMES=()
275	while IFS=$'\t' read -r r_mode r_name r_status _r_rc _r_el; do
276	  case "$r_status" in
277	    PASS) MODE_PASS[$r_mode]=$((MODE_PASS[$r_mode]+1)) ;;
278	    SKIP) MODE_SKIP[$r_mode]=$((MODE_SKIP[$r_mode]+1)) ;;
279	    FAIL) MODE_FAIL[$r_mode]=$((MODE_FAIL[$r_mode]+1));
280	          FAILED_NAMES+=("${r_name}[${r_mode}]") ;;
281	  esac
282	done < "$RESULTS_FILE"
283	
284	# Stream failed-test logs in workplan order so the user sees a
285	# deterministic post-run failure dump.
286	for w in "${WORKPLAN[@]}" "${SERIAL_PLAN[@]}"; do
287	  w_mode="${w%%|*}"
288	  w_rest="${w#*|}"
289	  w_name="${w_rest%%|*}"
290	  w_status=$(awk -F'\t' -v m="$w_mode" -v n="$w_name" \
291	                 '$1==m&&$2==n{print $3; exit}' "$RESULTS_FILE")
292	  if [[ "$w_status" == "FAIL" ]]; then
293	    echo
294	    echo "=== FAIL log: ${w_name}[${w_mode}] ==="
295	    cat "$LOG_DIR/$w_mode--$w_name.log"
296	  fi
297	done
298	
299	echo
300	marker_p=${MODE_PASS[marker]} marker_f=${MODE_FAIL[marker]} marker_s=${MODE_SKIP[marker]}
301	pc_p=${MODE_PASS[pc]}   pc_f=${MODE_FAIL[pc]}   pc_s=${MODE_SKIP[pc]}
302	neg_p=${MODE_PASS[neg]} neg_f=${MODE_FAIL[neg]} neg_s=${MODE_SKIP[neg]}
303	total_pass=$((marker_p + pc_p + neg_p))
304	total_fail=$((marker_f + pc_f + neg_f))
305	total_skip=$((marker_s + pc_s + neg_s))
306	step "summary: marker ${marker_p}p/${marker_f}f/${marker_s}s  pc ${pc_p}p/${pc_f}f/${pc_s}s  neg ${neg_p}p/${neg_f}f/${neg_s}s  total ${total_pass} passed, ${total_fail} failed, ${total_skip} skipped"
307	if (( total_fail > 0 )); then
308	  fail "failures: ${FAILED_NAMES[*]}"

2	# test_all.sh -- run the full andesim test surface. This is the entry point that
3	# replaced the former `andesim test` subcommand (which moved out of the binary).
4	#
5	# Phases (all run, in order, unless named explicitly):
6	#   unit      build/driver/andesim-*-test   the C++ driver unit tests
7	#   contract  tests/andes_sim/*.sh          driver feature + parity contracts
8	#   e2e       scripts/run_e2e.sh            hybrid qemu+vsim round-trips
9	#
10	# Usage:
11	#   scripts/test_all.sh [--dry-run] [unit|contract|e2e ...]
12	#
13	# --dry-run prints the plan without executing (and without building). The
14	# contract and e2e phases need built artifacts -- run scripts/build_all.sh
15	# first. FILTER / MODE / JOBS pass through to scripts/run_e2e.sh unchanged.
16	set -uo pipefail
17	
18	ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
19	
20	DRY_RUN=0
21	PHASES=()
22	for arg in "$@"; do
23	  case "$arg" in
24	    --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1 ;;
25	    unit|contract|e2e) PHASES+=("$arg") ;;
26	    *)
27	      echo "test_all.sh: unknown argument: $arg" >&2
28	      echo "usage: test_all.sh [--dry-run] [unit|contract|e2e ...]" >&2
29	      exit 2
30	      ;;
31	  esac
32	done
33	[ "${#PHASES[@]}" -eq 0 ] && PHASES=(unit contract e2e)
34	
35	step() { printf '\033[1;34m==>\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
36	ok()   { printf '\033[1;32m[ok]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
37	fail() { printf '\033[1;31m[FAIL]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; }
38	
39	pass=0
40	failed=0
41	declare -a FAILED_NAMES=()
42	
43	# run_case NAME CMD...  -- execute one case, tally it, dump its log on failure.
44	run_case() {
45	  local name="$1"; shift
46	  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then printf '  %s\n' "$name"; return; fi
47	  local log rc; log=$(mktemp)
48	  "$@" >"$log" 2>&1; rc=$?
49	  if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then
50	    ok "$name"; pass=$((pass + 1))
51	  else
52	    fail "$name (rc=$rc)"; failed=$((failed + 1)); FAILED_NAMES+=("$name")
53	    cat "$log"
54	  fi
55	  rm -f "$log"
56	}
57	
58	run_unit() {
59	  step "[unit] C++ driver unit tests"
60	  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then
61	    printf '  %s\n' "scripts/build_driver.sh" "build/driver/andesim-*-test (each)"
62	    return
63	  fi
64	  if ! bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null; then
65	    fail "[unit] build_driver.sh failed"; failed=$((failed + 1)); return
66	  fi
67	  shopt -s nullglob
68	  local bins=("$ROOT"/build/driver/andesim-*-test)
69	  shopt -u nullglob
70	  if [ "${#bins[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
71	    fail "[unit] no unit-test binaries under build/driver"; failed=$((failed + 1)); return
72	  fi
73	  local t
74	  for t in "${bins[@]}"; do run_case "[unit] $(basename "$t")" "$t"; done
75	}
76	
77	run_contract() {
78	  step "[contract] driver feature + parity contracts"
79	  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then
80	    printf '  %s\n' "tests/andes_sim/parity.sh" "tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_*.sh (each)"
81	    return
82	  fi
83	  local s
84	  for s in "$ROOT"/tests/andes_sim/parity.sh "$ROOT"/tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_*.sh; do
85	    [ -f "$s" ] || continue
86	    run_case "[contract] $(basename "$s")" bash "$s"
87	  done
88	}
89	
90	run_e2e() {
91	  step "[e2e] hybrid qemu+vsim round-trips"
92	  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then printf '  %s\n' "scripts/run_e2e.sh"; return; fi
93	  run_case "[e2e] run_e2e.sh" bash "$ROOT/scripts/run_e2e.sh"
94	}
95	
96	for p in "${PHASES[@]}"; do
97	  case "$p" in
98	    unit)     run_unit ;;
99	    contract) run_contract ;;
100	    e2e)      run_e2e ;;
101	  esac
102	done
103	
104	if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then
105	  echo
106	  echo "(dry-run: nothing executed)"
107	  exit 0
108	fi
109	
110	echo
111	step "summary: $pass passed, $failed failed"
112	if [ "$failed" -gt 0 ]; then
113	  fail "failed: ${FAILED_NAMES[*]}"
114	  exit 1
115	fi

8	# ROADMAP commands (profile, cluster, archive, replay, estimate) appear in no
9	# help at all. The cycle-accurate engine is presented as "vsim" everywhere --
10	# proven end to end with a fake engine that self-describes as "verilator" and
11	# must come back out as vsim:.

15	ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)

20	bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
21	
22	# has RE TEXT  -- TEXT must match RE ; missing RE TEXT -- TEXT must NOT match RE

26	# 1. release --help: a clear command TREE -- run/list/doctor are the major
27	# commands (column 0); each is followed by its indented subcommands (run's
28	# modes, list's targets); run carries its full option list with REQUIRED flags
29	# marked. No developer-commands section, no "verilator", no dev-only fixtures.

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# F9 contract: `run --mode hybrid` -- orchestrate a QEMU1 -> vsim handoff (no
3	# QEMU2) and print the one-line window-cycle figure for the marker | pc
4	# triggers. Three layers:
5	#
6	#   1. unit (fast, no spawn): the elf-syms boundary resolver, hybrid_trigger
7	#      (CLI -> Trigger, incl. pc symbol resolution), the trigger->argv mapping
8	#      (plan-test), and the new CLI flags (cli-test).
9	#   2. validation error paths via the real binary, all exiting BEFORE any spawn:
10	#      missing ELF, pc without boundaries, an undefined pc symbol, simpoint
11	#      (F11, not yet), and an unknown trigger.
12	#   3. real handoff + golden parity (guarded): run marker/pc through both
13	#      ./hsim.py (the Python golden) and andesim and assert identical window
14	#      cycle numbers, plus the new output format. Skipped when the qemu/vsim/
15	#      plugin artifacts or the golden driver are not built.
16	#
17	# pc uses handoff_roundtrip.elf's own markers as the boundaries (_start =
18	# the enter marker 0x100000, 0x10000c = the exit marker), so pc reproduces marker's
19	# switch points exactly -- and exercises BOTH symbol and 0x resolution.
20	set -uo pipefail
21	
22	SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
23	ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
24	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"
25	
26	BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
27	ELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/handoff_roundtrip.elf"  # asm fixture
28	CELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/rt_c_matmul.elf"       # C fixture (needs shared mmap)
29	ENG=vsim:ax45mpv_premium  # the engine ./hsim.py resolves by default
30	
31	bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
32	
33	# 1. unit tests (the F9 pure cores)
34	for t in elf-syms hybrid plan cli; do
35	  "$ROOT/build/driver/andesim-$t-test" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
36	    || fail "unit test andesim-$t-test failed"
37	done
38	echo "[ok] unit: elf-syms, hybrid_trigger, trigger->argv (plan), CLI flags"
39	
40	# 2. validation error paths -- real binary, but every case errors before a spawn
41	# (expect: assert rc + output regex; shared helper from tests/lib/log.sh)
42	expect 2 'ELF not found'        "$BIN" run --mode hybrid /no/such.elf
43	expect 2 'engine args go after' "$BIN" run --mode hybrid a.elf b.elf
44	expect 2 'trigger.*is required' "$BIN" run --mode hybrid "$ELF"
45	expect 2 'requires --pc-start'  "$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger pc "$ELF"
46	expect 2 'not defined' "$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger pc \
47	  --pc-start nope_xyz --pc-end _start "$ELF"
48	expect 2 'F11'              "$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger simpoint "$ELF"
49	expect 2 'unknown trigger'  "$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger bogus "$ELF"
50	expect 2 'requires --kanata' "$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker \
51	  --objdump /tmp/o "$ELF"
52	echo "[ok] validation: missing ELF, missing --trigger, pc boundaries, bad symbol, simpoint/unknown trigger, kanata/objdump"
53	
54	# 3. real handoff + golden parity (guarded on built artifacts)
55	QEMU="$ROOT/build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64"
56	SIM="$ROOT/verilator/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
57	PLUGIN="$ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so"
58	if [ -x "$QEMU" ] && [ -x "$SIM" ] && [ -f "$PLUGIN" ] && [ -x "$ROOT/hsim.py" ]; then
59	  # Pull the window/kernel cycle integer from either driver's "] N  (vsim..."
60	  # line (golden marker/pc say "kernel_cycles", andes says "window_cycles";
61	  # the number's position is identical).
62	  cyc() { grep -oE '\] [0-9]+  \(' | grep -oE '[0-9]+' | head -1; }
63	  check_parity() {  # LABEL GOLDEN_NUM ANDES_NUM
64	    [ -n "$2" ] || fail "$1: golden produced no cycle number"
65	    [ -n "$3" ] || fail "$1: andesim produced no cycle number"
66	    [ "$2" = "$3" ] || fail "$1: cycle mismatch golden=$2 andes=$3"
67	    echo "[ok] $1 parity: $3 cycles (golden == andesim)"
68	  }
69	
70	  # marker -- also assert the new output format (window_cycles + PASS line)
71	  GO=$(cd "$ROOT" && timeout 180 ./hsim.py run --mode marker "$ELF" 2>&1 | cyc)
72	  AO=$(timeout 180 "$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENG" "$ELF" 2>&1)
73	  printf '%s\n' "$AO" | grep -Eq '^\[marker window_cycles\] [0-9]+  \(vsim mcycle=' \
74	    || fail "marker: missing window_cycles line: $AO"
75	  printf '%s\n' "$AO" | grep -Eq '^PASS: --mode hybrid --trigger marker ' \
76	    || fail "marker: missing PASS line: $AO"
77	  check_parity marker "$GO" "$(printf '%s\n' "$AO" | cyc)"
78	
79	  # marker on a C fixture -- the stack/heap + main()'s frame must survive the
80	  # handoff through the shared mmap (asm fixtures are self-contained; this is
81	  # the "+ C fixtures" half of the done-when).
82	  GO=$(cd "$ROOT" && timeout 180 ./hsim.py run --mode marker "$CELF" 2>&1 | cyc)
83	  AO=$(timeout 180 "$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENG" "$CELF" 2>&1 | cyc)
84	  check_parity marker-c "$GO" "$AO"
85	
86	  # pc -- symbol start (_start) + 0x end (the exit marker)
87	  GO=$(cd "$ROOT" && timeout 180 ./hsim.py run --mode pc \
88	        --pc-start _start --pc-end 0x10000c "$ELF" 2>&1 | cyc)
89	  AO=$(timeout 180 "$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger pc --engine "$ENG" \
90	        --pc-start _start --pc-end 0x10000c "$ELF" 2>&1 | cyc)
91	  check_parity pc "$GO" "$AO"
92	
93	  # kanata ROI trace forwards onto the vsim leg and writes a non-empty file.
94	  KAN=$(mktemp); rm -f "$KAN"
95	  timeout 180 "$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENG" \
96	    --kanata "$KAN" "$ELF" >/dev/null 2>&1
97	  [ -s "$KAN" ] || fail "kanata: trace file empty/missing after marker run"
98	  echo "[ok] kanata: marker run wrote a non-empty ROI trace ($(wc -l <"$KAN") lines)"
99	  rm -f "$KAN"
100	else
101	  echo "[skip] real handoff parity: need built qemu+vsim+plugin and ./hsim"
102	fi
103	
104	ok "F9 run --mode hybrid (marker|pc)"

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# End-to-end harness: QEMU 1 + plugin -> vsim (2-phase, no QEMU2 handback).
3	#
4	# Memory between QEMU and vsim is shared via an /dev/shm-backed mmap
5	# (128 MB). Works for both asm fixtures (handoff_roundtrip, rt_*) and
6	# C-level fixtures (rt_c_*). C fixtures require shared mmap so the
7	# stack/heap survives handoffs; asm fixtures don't need it but run
8	# fine with it.
9	#
10	# Env:
11	#   FIXTURE         REQUIRED. .elf name under tests/fixtures/ (no .elf suffix).
12	#   TRIGGER_MODE    marker | pc (default marker).
13	#   ROI_START       pc mode switch-in PC: a 0x address or a symbol in
14	#                   $VSIM_ELF. If BOTH ROI_START and ROI_END are unset, they
15	#                   are auto-derived from the fixture's ROI marker HINTs via
16	#                   objdump (see roi_markers_from_disasm) -- the bulk runner
17	#                   relies on this; ./andesim run always passes them explicitly.
18	#   ROI_END         pc mode switch-out PC, same forms / same auto-derivation.
19	#   TIMEOUT         vsim leg timeout in seconds (default 60).
20	#   CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC=1   assert mcycle/minstret strictly increased
21	#                              between QEMU 1's drain and vsim's drain.
22	#   CHECK_PRIV=<0|1|3>         assert both drained state files carry this
23	#                              privilege (L6: 0=U, 1=S, 3=M).
24	#   WARMUP_ICOUNT              gem5-style warmup window. When set and > 0,
25	#                              passes --vsim-warmup-icount K to vsim and
26	#                              prints a [warmup] line carrying the captured
27	#                              (mcycle_at_measure_start, minstret_at_measure_start)
28	#                              pair from the drained state file.
29	#   VSIM_BIN, VSIM_QEMU, VSIM_PLUGIN, VSIM_ELF, NM  override built paths.
30	#   QEMU_CPU        -cpu argument for both QEMU legs (default
31	#                   andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512, pairing the default vsim
32	#                   engine). Override together with VSIM_BIN to run a
33	#                   fixture on another engine, e.g. the S/U-capable
34	#                   ax66_makatau for the rt_priv_* fixtures (the default
35	#                   ax45mpv_premium RTL is M-mode-only).
36	
37	set -euo pipefail
38	
39	SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
40	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/paths.sh"
41	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/roi.sh"
42	
43	FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:?FIXTURE env var is required (e.g. FIXTURE=rt_c_hello)}"
44	TIMEOUT="${TIMEOUT:-60}"
45	TRIGGER_MODE="${TRIGGER_MODE:-marker}"
46	QEMU_CPU="${QEMU_CPU:-andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512}"
47	
48	hybrid_resolve_paths
49	
50	NM="${NM:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm}}"
51	NM="${NM:-riscv64-unknown-elf-nm}"
52	
53	case "$TRIGGER_MODE" in
54	  marker) ;;
55	  pc)
56	    if ! command -v "$NM" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
57	      echo "skip[$FIXTURE pc]: nm not found at $NM"
58	      exit 77
59	    fi
60	    # ROI_START / ROI_END name the two switch PCs (0x address or symbol in
61	    # $VSIM_ELF). ./andesim run always passes them explicitly. When a caller
62	    # leaves BOTH unset (e.g. the bulk runner scripts/run_e2e.sh), derive them
63	    # from the fixture's ROI marker HINTs via objdump, so pc mode needs no
64	    # per-fixture config and no planted boundary symbols. A partial set or a
65	    # derivation miss falls through to roi_resolve_pair's required-vars error.
66	    if [ -z "${ROI_START:-}" ] && [ -z "${ROI_END:-}" ]; then
67	      OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}}"
68	      OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}"
69	      if command -v "$OBJDUMP" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
70	         && MARKERS=$(roi_markers_from_disasm "$("$OBJDUMP" -d "$VSIM_ELF")"); then
71	        ROI_START="0x${MARKERS%% *}"
72	        ROI_END="0x${MARKERS##* }"
73	        export ROI_START ROI_END
74	      fi
75	    fi
76	    NM_OUT=$("$NM" --defined-only "$VSIM_ELF")
77	    roi_resolve_pair "$NM_OUT" "$FIXTURE pc" || exit 1
78	    ;;
79	  *)
80	    echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: unknown TRIGGER_MODE=$TRIGGER_MODE (use marker|pc)"
81	    exit 1
82	    ;;
83	esac
84	
85	# 128 MB program RAM matches the QEMU virt machine default. L26/F2: the
86	# physical mmap reserves one V-scratch page (HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES =
87	# 32 * HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX) ABOVE the program's RAM, so the V-transport
88	# scratch (vsim parks it at the mmap top page) sits past anything the program
89	# can address. Mirrors the andesim driver (shm.cpp physical_mmap_bytes).
90	# Read HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX from the shared ABI so this tracks the header
91	# (the ceiling moved 64 -> 128 once already) instead of hardcoding it.
92	VLEN_BYTES_MAX=$(awk '/^#define HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX/ {print $3}' \
93	  "$SCRIPT_DIR/../include/hybrid/state_abi.h")
94	[ -n "$VLEN_BYTES_MAX" ] || { echo "e2e: cannot read HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX from state_abi.h" >&2; exit 1; }
95	PROGRAM_SIZE=$((128 * 1024 * 1024))
96	V_SCRATCH_BYTES=$((32 * VLEN_BYTES_MAX))
97	SHARED_SIZE=$((PROGRAM_SIZE + V_SCRATCH_BYTES))
98	SHARED_MEM=$(mktemp -p /dev/shm vsim-e2e-shared.XXXXXX)
99	STATE_QEMU=$(mktemp)
100	STATE_VSIM=$(mktemp)
101	SIM_LOG=$(mktemp)
102	trap 'rm -f "$SHARED_MEM" "$STATE_QEMU" "$STATE_VSIM" "$SIM_LOG"' EXIT
103	truncate -s "$SHARED_SIZE" "$SHARED_MEM"
104	
105	PLUGIN_ARGS="outfile=$STATE_QEMU"
106	VSIM_TRIG_ARGS=()
107	if [ "$TRIGGER_MODE" = "pc" ]; then
108	  PLUGIN_ARGS="$PLUGIN_ARGS,enter_pc=0x$ENTER_PC"
109	  VSIM_TRIG_ARGS=(--hybrid-exit-pc "0x$EXIT_PC")
110	fi
111	
112	# F21: forward --vsim-warmup-icount when caller asked for a warmup window.
113	VSIM_WARMUP_ARGS=()
114	if [ "${WARMUP_ICOUNT:-0}" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
115	  VSIM_WARMUP_ARGS=(--vsim-warmup-icount "$WARMUP_ICOUNT")
116	fi
117	
118	# Optional ROI kanata logging: hsim sets KANATA_FILE (and optionally
119	# OBJDUMP_FILE) when the user passes --kanata. vsim's --kanata-roi auto-
120	# derives the window from the resume PC and the unique exit PC.
121	VSIM_KANATA_ARGS=()
122	if [ -n "${KANATA_FILE:-}" ]; then
123	  VSIM_KANATA_ARGS+=(--kanata "$KANATA_FILE" --kanata-roi)
124	  if [ -n "${OBJDUMP_FILE:-}" ]; then
125	    VSIM_KANATA_ARGS+=(--objdump "$OBJDUMP_FILE")
126	  fi
127	fi
128	
129	echo "[$FIXTURE 1/2 mode=$TRIGGER_MODE] QEMU 1: drain entry state"
130	set +e
131	"$VSIM_QEMU" \
132	  -object "memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=$SHARED_MEM,size=$SHARED_SIZE" \
133	  -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \
134	  -cpu "$QEMU_CPU" \
135	  -nographic \
136	  -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
137	  -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
138	  -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,$PLUGIN_ARGS" </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1
139	QEMU1_RC=$?
140	set -e
141	
142	if [ "$QEMU1_RC" -ne 200 ]; then
143	  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: QEMU 1 expected exit 200 on drain, got $QEMU1_RC"
144	  exit 1
145	fi
146	
147	if [ ! -s "$STATE_QEMU" ]; then
148	  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: QEMU 1 did not produce state"
149	  exit 1
150	fi
151	
152	echo "[$FIXTURE 2/2 mode=$TRIGGER_MODE] vsim: resume + drain"
153	set +e
154	timeout "$TIMEOUT" "$VSIM_BIN" "$VSIM_ELF" \
155	  --resume-from-qemu "$STATE_QEMU" \
156	  --handoff-out "$STATE_VSIM" \
157	  --shared-mem-path "$SHARED_MEM" \
158	  --shared-mem-size "$SHARED_SIZE" \
159	  --shared-mem-base 0x00000000 \
160	  "${VSIM_TRIG_ARGS[@]}" \
161	  "${VSIM_KANATA_ARGS[@]}" \
162	  "${VSIM_WARMUP_ARGS[@]}" </dev/null >"$SIM_LOG" 2>&1
163	VSIM_RC=$?
164	set -e
165	
166	# vsim drained on the exit trigger and exited 200 (kExitHandoffToQemu).
167	# Anything else is a hard failure: the cycle figure is only valid when vsim
168	# drained cleanly.
169	if [ "$VSIM_RC" -ne 200 ]; then
170	  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: vsim expected exit 200 (drain), got $VSIM_RC"
171	  echo "--- sim log ---"
172	  cat "$SIM_LOG"
173	  exit 1
174	fi
175	
176	# Kernel cycles (always) + opt-in monotonic check. Offsets locked by
177	# state_abi_check.h (mcycle@624, minstret@632). vsim restores mcycle from
178	# QEMU 1's drain then counts real clock cycles, so vsim_mcycle - qemu1_mcycle
179	# is the measured region's cycle count. Runs before the RC gate so the
180	# verdict is independent of any downstream-phase failure.
181	read_u64_le() { od -A n -j "$1" -N 8 -t u8 "$2" | tr -d ' \n'; }
182	if [ -s "$STATE_VSIM" ] && [ -s "$STATE_QEMU" ]; then
183	  Q1_MCYCLE=$(read_u64_le 624 "$STATE_QEMU")
184	  Q1_MINST=$(read_u64_le  632 "$STATE_QEMU")
185	  V_MCYCLE=$(read_u64_le  624 "$STATE_VSIM")
186	  V_MINST=$(read_u64_le   632 "$STATE_VSIM")
187	  echo "[$FIXTURE kernel_cycles] $((V_MCYCLE - Q1_MCYCLE))  (vsim mcycle=$V_MCYCLE - qemu1 mcycle=$Q1_MCYCLE)"
188	  # F21: when WARMUP_ICOUNT is set, surface the snapshot pair so callers
189	  # can verify the warmup window without re-parsing the state file.
190	  # Offsets locked by include/hybrid/state_abi_check.h (F13, ceiling 128):
191	  #   mcycle_at_measure_start@5440, minstret_at_measure_start@5448.
192	  if [ "${WARMUP_ICOUNT:-0}" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
193	    MS_MC=$(read_u64_le 5440 "$STATE_VSIM")
194	    MS_MI=$(read_u64_le 5448 "$STATE_VSIM")
195	    echo "[$FIXTURE warmup] K=$WARMUP_ICOUNT mcycle_at_measure_start=$MS_MC minstret_at_measure_start=$MS_MI"
196	  fi
197	  # L6: privilege survives the handoff. priv@24 locked by state_abi_check.h.
198	  if [ -n "${CHECK_PRIV:-}" ]; then
199	    Q1_PRIV=$(read_u64_le 24 "$STATE_QEMU")
200	    V_PRIV=$(read_u64_le  24 "$STATE_VSIM")
201	    echo "[$FIXTURE priv] qemu1=$Q1_PRIV vsim=$V_PRIV expected=$CHECK_PRIV"
202	    if [ "$Q1_PRIV" != "$CHECK_PRIV" ] || [ "$V_PRIV" != "$CHECK_PRIV" ]; then
203	      echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: drained priv mismatch (expected $CHECK_PRIV)"
204	      exit 1
205	    fi
206	  fi
207	  if [ "${CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC:-0}" = "1" ]; then
208	    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] qemu1: mcycle=$Q1_MCYCLE minstret=$Q1_MINST"
209	    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] vsim:  mcycle=$V_MCYCLE minstret=$V_MINST"
210	    if [ "$V_MCYCLE" -le "$Q1_MCYCLE" ]; then
211	      echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: mcycle not strictly increasing across vsim"
212	      exit 1
213	    fi
214	    if [ "$V_MINST" -le "$Q1_MINST" ]; then
215	      echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: minstret not strictly increasing across vsim"
216	      exit 1
217	    fi
218	    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] PASS: strictly increasing"
219	  fi
220	fi
221	
222	echo "[$FIXTURE PASS] 2-phase handoff complete (QEMU 1 drain -> vsim drain)"
223

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Oracle exit-drain contract (verify_oracle F1): a pure-QEMU run drains
3	# hybrid_state_v1 at the ROI EXIT boundary, producing the reference state the
4	# differential verifier compares against the vsim drain.
5	#
6	# Semantics: arm on the exit boundary's exec callback, drain on the NEXT exec
7	# callback. That callback fires before its own insn executes, so the captured
8	# state is "after the boundary insn retired" -- exactly what vsim's exit drain
9	# records (DPC = next insn to execute) -- and the reported pc is the next
10	# insn's vaddr, correct even for a branching boundary insn.
11	#
12	# Cases:
13	#   1. exit_marker=1  -- arm on `slti x0, x0, 0x5A1`; pc must be marker+4
14	#                        (NOT enter-marker+4: the ENTER marker must not drain).
15	#   2. exit_pc=0x...  -- arm on the boundary vaddr; same expectation when the
16	#                        boundary is the (fall-through) exit marker.
17	#   3. drain_pc=0x... -- sample at a later, caller-chosen pc instead of the
18	#                        very next insn. The differential harness passes
19	#                        vsim's actual halt pc here: vsim's DMI halt lands a
20	#                        variable 0-3 insns past the trigger, and both sides
21	#                        must sample the SAME architectural point.
22	#   4. exit_marker=1,icount=N -- install error: oracle mode is exclusive with
23	#                        the other trigger modes; drain_pc requires oracle
24	#                        mode.
25	#
26	# Required environment (auto-detected with sensible defaults):
27	#   VSIM_QEMU    qemu-system-riscv64
28	#   VSIM_PLUGIN  libhybrid_handoff.so
29	#   FIXTURE      a marker-carrying fixture (default: rt_c_hello)
30	
31	set -uo pipefail
32	
33	SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
34	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"
35	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/roi.sh"
36	
37	FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-rt_c_hello}"
38	hybrid_resolve_paths
39	
40	OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}}"
41	OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}"
42	command -v "$OBJDUMP" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "skip[oracle_exit_drain]: no objdump"; exit 77; }
43	
44	MARKERS=$(roi_markers_from_disasm "$("$OBJDUMP" -d "$VSIM_ELF")") \
45	  || { echo "FAIL[oracle_exit_drain]: no ROI markers in $VSIM_ELF"; exit 1; }
46	EXIT_PC="0x${MARKERS##* }"
47	# The exit marker is a 4-byte NOP that falls through, so the first insn
48	# executed after it retires sits at marker+4.
49	WANT_PC=$(printf '0x%x' $((EXIT_PC + 4)))
50	
51	STATE=$(mktemp)
